speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the mechanism of injury: were you wearing a seatbelt, and did you experience significant pain or an audible "pop" in your right groin at the moment of impact? Also, can you describe the specific position your right leg is currently resting in?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since you have severe right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision, did you notice any difficulty moving your right hip or an inability to rotate your leg inward or outward? Also, can you tell me if the pain radiates down your leg or if you are feeling any numbness in your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hip_X-Ray_ap_lateral. This specific leg position—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is highly characteristic of a hip dislocation; have you lost all sensation in your right foot or had any trouble moving your toes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray Findings: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip. Right_hip_X-Ray_ap_lateral Findings: Confirms posterior dislocation of the right hip with the femoral head displaced posteriorly relative to the acetabulum. No evidence of fracture of the femoral neck or acetabulum.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation. Based on the classic "shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated" deformity following a rear-end collision, this is a medical emergency requiring immediate closed reduction. Please proceed to the OR immediately.
